person.name: Samuel Akinwumi Adeniji
person.headline: AI for Healthcare · Multimodal Medical AI · Medical Image Analysis
person.bio: I'm an M.S. student in Engineering AI at **Carnegie Mellon University Africa**. I work on **multimodal medical AI**: models that combine images such as pathology slides, CT and MRI with molecular and clinical data. I care about whether each input really helps, whether the model's evidence can be checked, and whether it still works at a new hospital, especially in low-resource and African health settings.

projects.title: Scan-Specific Information in Compressed 3D CT Vision–Language Models
projects.org: Language and Spatial Laboratories, Carnegie Mellon University
projects.summary: A vision–language pipeline that writes radiology reports from 3D chest CT, compressing each volume into a small budget of visual tokens. Swapping scans between reports showed the model often wrote template-like reports that barely depended on the scan, so the project now measures how much scan-specific information survives compression, and how to keep it.
projects.summary_plain: A vision–language pipeline that writes radiology reports from 3D chest CT, compressing each volume into a small budget of visual tokens. Swapping scans between reports showed the model often wrote template-like reports that barely depended on the scan, so the project now measures how much scan-specific information survives compression, and how to keep it.
projects.note: Research internship with Prof. Prasenjit Mitra (May–Aug 2026), continuing.
projects.note_plain: Research internship with Prof. Prasenjit Mitra (May–Aug 2026), continuing.
bullets: Built a full pipeline for 3D chest-CT report generation on CT-RATE. A frozen slice encoder feeds a Perceiver-style stage that condenses each slice to 32 latents, an instruction-conditioned stage condenses the slices into a fixed budget of visual tokens, and a LoRA-adapted language model writes the report.
Built a multi-task instruction pipeline with a 368-test suite, evaluated across six token budgets from 16 to 512, and a step that selects 3D viewing planes inside the volume.

Diagnostic tests (swapping scans between reports) showed the model often wrote template-like reports even when text metrics looked reasonable; the project is now being rebuilt around measuring and keeping scan-specific information (arXiv report planned, then ICCV 2027).

projects.title: FPN-Mamba: Linear-Time Bidirectional State Space Feature Pyramids for Small-Lesion Brain MRI Classification
projects.site_status: Accepted · NeurIPS 2026 Africa in AI Workshop
projects.summary: Feature pyramid plus bidirectional Mamba for small brain-metastasis screening on UCSF-BMSR. It outperforms a self-attention baseline (InceptentionNet) on AUC (0.982 vs 0.897) and smallest-lesion recall (0.870 vs 0.788) across 5 seeds × 3 folds, and is 3.7× faster per step than a matched attention mixer at 512 px.
projects.summary_plain: Feature pyramid plus bidirectional Mamba for small brain-metastasis screening on UCSF-BMSR. It outperforms a self-attention baseline (InceptentionNet) on AUC (0.982 vs 0.897) and smallest-lesion recall (0.870 vs 0.788) across 5 seeds × 3 folds, and is 3.7× faster per step than a matched attention mixer at 512 px.
bullets: Combined a feature pyramid network with bidirectional Mamba state-space blocks to detect small brain metastases in MRI, in linear time.

Against a re-implemented InceptentionNet (5 seeds × 3 folds), reaches AUC 0.982 vs 0.897 and smallest-lesion recall 0.870 vs 0.788 (all p < 0.02), and trains 3.7× faster per step than a matched self-attention design at 512 pixels.
Accepted at the Africa in AI Workshop, NeurIPS 2026 — [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=te52LwNBSf).
bullets_plain: Combined a feature pyramid network with bidirectional Mamba state-space blocks to detect small brain metastases in MRI, in linear time.

projects.title: Investigating White Blood Cells as a Source of False-Positive Malaria Parasite Detection in African Blood-Smear Images
projects.readme_title: Where Do Malaria Detector False Positives Come From?
projects.summary: A controlled study of two YOLOv12s detectors on 6,593 thick-smear images from Uganda and Ghana (Lacuna dataset), using seven spatial and statistical analyses. The evidence does not support white blood cells as a systematic source of false positives, and points mitigation toward staining and preparation variability.
projects.summary_plain: A controlled study of two YOLOv12s detectors on 6,593 thick-smear images from Uganda and Ghana (Lacuna dataset), using seven spatial and statistical analyses. The evidence does not support white blood cells as a systematic source of false positives, and points mitigation toward staining and preparation variability.
bullets: Ran a controlled study on 6,593 Giemsa-stained thick blood-smear images from Uganda and Ghana, comparing detectors trained with and without white blood cell labels; about 95% of false positives were background detections, with no class confusions.

Seven spatial and statistical analyses (including Ripley's Cross-K, DBSCAN and Mann–Whitney U), each comparing false positives with the model's own correct detections, did not support the belief that white blood cells cause false-positive parasite detections, pointing to staining variability instead.
Accepted for oral presentation at the MIRASOL Workshop, MICCAI 2026 — [paper](https://papers.miccai.org/miccai-2026-sat/MIRASOL_018.html) · [arXiv:2609.29663](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29663).

projects.title: ClinFuse: Multimodal Cancer Survival Prediction
projects.summary: Survival prediction that adds clinical variables (stage, grade, age) to a whole-slide image and RNA model (building on SurvPath), trained to rank patients with a Cox loss and tested with whole hospitals held out. Without stage, it reaches c-index 0.712 vs 0.601 (kidney) and 0.671 vs 0.556 (endometrial) against SurvPath, and the ordering holds on external CPTAC hospitals. Team project; my part was data processing and training on the Narval cluster.

projects.title: Fetal Ultrasound Plane Classification: Bias and Ethics Across Datasets
projects.summary: A project classifying standard fetal ultrasound planes (brain, abdomen, femur, thorax and others) using public datasets. My part is measuring bias across the datasets and setting out the ethical issues, following the review of public fetal ultrasound datasets by Fiorentino et al. (npj Digital Medicine, 2025).

projects.title: LLM Evaluation Harness for a Maternal-Health Chatbot (Jacaranda Health)
projects.summary: An M.S. capstone with Jacaranda Health, building automated tests that run before a new version of their maternal-health SMS assistant is released. projects.title: Condition-Aware Intensive Care Unit Early-Warning System
projects.summary: Diagnosis-conditioned early-warning models on MIMIC-IV, benchmarking six sequence architectures at 1–3 h horizons. The best model (BiLSTM + attention, ROC-AUC 0.76) is served as a Dockerized FastAPI + WebSocket streaming service, with limitations documented up front.
projects.summary_plain: Diagnosis-conditioned early-warning models on MIMIC-IV, benchmarking six sequence architectures at 1–3 h horizons. The best model (BiLSTM + attention, ROC-AUC 0.76) is served as a Dockerized FastAPI + WebSocket streaming service, with limitations documented up front.
bullets: Benchmarked six diagnosis-conditioned sequence models (LSTM, GRU, TCN, BiLSTM with attention, Transformer, TFT-style) for deterioration risk on MIMIC-IV intensive care data; the best, a BiLSTM with attention, reaches ROC-AUC 0.76.
Deployed it as a Dockerized FastAPI service with WebSocket streaming inference, built for reproducibility under PhysioNet data governance.
